title: How to play
subtitle: Explore Grugnetto’s worlds, claim the best Places and be the last player still in the game.

objective.title: Goal
paragraphs: Choose between {{minCpuOpponents}} and {{maxCpuOpponents}} opponents, for a total of {{minPlayers}} to {{maxPlayers}} players.
Everyone starts with {{startingCash}} coins. The last player still in the game wins.

turn.title: Your turn
paragraphs: Roll two dice and move by their total. Whenever you pass Grugnetto’s Home, collect {{passStartSalary}} coins.
If you roll doubles, resolve the space and roll again. Three doubles in a row send you straight to Base Camp.

places.title: Places and Revenue
paragraphs: When you land on an unclaimed Place, you may buy it for the listed price. If you do not buy it, the Place goes to auction.
When you land on another player’s Place, pay its Revenue. A pledged Place does not collect Revenue.

On the board, an unclaimed Place shows its price in green. Once it has an owner it shows the Revenue you pay when you land there instead: brown, gold if it has Embellishments, and struck-through grey if it is pledged (the Revenue it would collect again once redeemed). For special Places the Revenue is a multiple of the dice roll, such as ×3.

worlds.title: Worlds and Embellishments
paragraphs: The board contains {{worldCount}} Worlds with {{placesPerWorld}} Places each. Once you own every Place in a World, their base Revenue doubles as long as none of them is pledged.
A completed World can be embellished. Each Place can have up to {{maxEmbellishments}} Embellishments, each bought for its listed cost. You do not have to build evenly across the World.

portalsServices.title: Portals and Special Places
paragraphs: The {{portalCount}} Portals can be bought like other Places. The more Portals you own, the more Revenue each Portal earns.
The {{specialPlaceCount}} Special Places work as a pair: their Revenue is based on the dice total and increases if you own both.

baseCamp.title: Base Camp
paragraphs: At Base Camp you may pay {{detentionFee}} coins and leave immediately, or try to roll doubles.

You have up to {{detentionTurns}} turns to succeed. If the second attempt is not doubles, you pay {{detentionFee}} coins and move by that roll anyway. Rolling doubles to leave does not grant another roll.

auctions.title: Auctions
paragraphs: Whenever an unclaimed Place is not bought, every player still in the game may join the auction.
Enter the most you are willing to spend. The game compares all bids and awards the Place to the winner, who may pay less than their maximum. Enter 0 to sit out.

trades.title: Trading
paragraphs: During your turn you may propose a trade to another player, offering Places, asking for others and adding coins from either side.
Places from a World cannot be traded while that World has any Embellishments. Sell all of them first.

pledges.title: Pledges
paragraphs: You may pledge one of your Places and receive {{pledgePercent}}% of its price. Redeeming it costs {{redeemPercent}}% of the original price.
Before pledging a Place from a World, every Embellishment in that World must be sold. Selling an Embellishment returns {{sellEmbellishmentPercent}}% of its cost.

events.title: Adventures and Setbacks
paragraphs: Adventure and Setback spaces make you draw a card. It may give or take coins, move you around the board, send you to a Portal or Base Camp, or affect your Embellishments.
Just follow the card: the game applies its effect immediately.

debts.title: When you run short of coins
paragraphs: If you owe more than your current cash, the game automatically tries to raise the money: it sells your Embellishments first, then pledges your Places.
If that is still not enough, you are eliminated. If the debt was owed to another player, your Places pass to that player; otherwise they become unclaimed again.

winning.title: Winning the game
paragraphs: Keep buying, embellishing, trading and managing your coins. As soon as only one player remains, the game ends and that player wins.
